source.title: EXAdam: The Power of Adaptive Cross-Moments

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer results on held-out data using benchmark tasks, but does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons or tuning setup in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper's EXAdam-versus-other-optimizers results are excluded because EXAdam is the study's own new method. Rows record the reported Adam and AdamW comparisons with SGD, which bear directly on V4. Other optimizer values are not cataloged here.
record.test_reason: The study's baseline comparisons measure Adam and AdamW held-out performance against momentum SGD on image classification and character-level language modeling, bearing on V4. Its shared or default hyperparameter recipes do not reproduce the optimizer-specific tuning underlying V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report improved CIFAR-10 performance for EXAdam and competitive MinGPT validation loss, while calling for broader empirical validation. Their language-model results do not establish uniform validation superiority: EXAdam's final validation loss is worse than Adam's and AdamW's.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizers on CIFAR-10 and a Shakespeare MinGPT task. The image experiment uses the same learning rate across optimizers; the language experiment uses each optimizer's default hyperparameters. It does not use Wilson et al.'s benchmark suite or broad tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer hyperparameter setup differs by experiment: shared learning rate on CIFAR-10, default hyperparameters for the language experiment.
record.code_released: https://github.com/ (the paper says the code is available on GitHub but gives no URL in the supplied text)
record.problems: Single CIFAR-10 CNN with one stated seed; only one learning rate is used for all image optimizers, and the paper says this may not be optimal for each. The language experiment uses default hyperparameters and a small dataset where overfitting is considered likely. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded EXAdam's own results and results for other optimizers because the study's own new method compared with other methods is not a row under the row rules. Table 1 training and validation metrics were also left out; the selected held-out results directly compare Adam or AdamW with SGD.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; comparable training performance; controlled decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language modeling.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with generalization gaps, norms, and margins.
Removing memorized examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

missing.what: AdamW's MinGPT validation loss at iteration 8000 is 1.494 versus momentum SGD's 2.684; training losses are 1.184 and 2.665. This directly relevant AdamW comparison is not recorded or explicitly declared omitted.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. The results qualify the scope of optimizer rankings under these recipes; they do not refute V4's qualified claim about frequently observed disadvantages after limited tuning. One stated seed and no uncertainty estimates limit the evidence. Table 2 values support the extracted rows, but nearby prose gives inconsistent EXAdam improvement arithmetic.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Broader optimizer tuning, explicit weight-decay settings, switching from Adam to SGD, and other image or language benchmarks.
Batch-size comparisons and changes to the training recipe.
Dropout comparisons and its interaction with data augmentation.
Sharpness, norm or margin measures and their relation to generalization gaps.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: CNN trained with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 using Adam; learning rate 0.0001 for all optimizers.
rows.note: Adam's reported test accuracy is higher than the SGD comparator, contrary to V4's expected direction.
rows.check: Values are correct. Describe the budget as 100 epochs: Table 1 labels it that way, although the prose says iterations. The shared initial learning rate of 0.0001 used ReduceLROnPlateau. SGD training accuracy was only 54.67%, versus Adam's 93.12%, so this comparison does not isolate generalization after comparable fitting.

rows.subject: CNN trained with AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 using AdamW; learning rate 0.0001 for all optimizers.
rows.note: AdamW's reported test accuracy is higher than the SGD comparator, contrary to V4's expected direction.
rows.check: Values are correct. The budget is 100 epochs in Table 1, with a shared initial learning rate and ReduceLROnPlateau. AdamW training accuracy was 93.83%, versus SGD's 54.67%. AdamW's advantage does not establish recovery through decoupled weight decay because weight-decay settings and a controlled decay comparison are absent.

rows.subject: MinGPT trained with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Shakespeare text; optimizers used default hyperparameters.
rows.note: Lower validation loss for Adam than SGD with Momentum; the paper notes the dataset is relatively small and overfitting is likely.
rows.check: Values are correct. The setup says default optimizer hyperparameters but also lists a learning rate of 0.0001; preserve this ambiguity. This is character-level modeling. Adam's training loss was 1.185 versus SGD's 2.665, so the validation comparison accompanies substantially different training performance.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 CNN, 100 epochs, shared initial learning rate 0.0001 with ReduceLROnPlateau
relationships.reason: R1–R2 report Adam/AdamW test accuracies of 89.66%/89.71% versus SGD's 43.13%; adaptive methods win under this recipe, but SGD also fits training data much worse and optimizer-specific tuning was not performed.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam and AdamW accuracy exceeded SGD, which also fit training data worse; these comparisons remain unverified and lacked optimizer-specific tuning.

relationships.condition: Shakespeare character-level MinGPT at 8000 iterations under the reported default/shared-learning-rate setup
relationships.reason: R3 reports Adam validation loss 1.505 versus SGD's 2.684; the text also reports AdamW at 1.494, missing from the rows. These adaptive advantages accompany much lower training losses without optimizer-specific tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam and AdamW validation losses were lower than SGD alongside lower training losses, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
